newsitem.title: USA: Spanish prime minister seeks NATO recognition.
newsitem.headline: Spanish prime minister seeks NATO recognition.

text.p: Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar called on Tuesday for "clear" recognition of his country's growing role in NATO.
Arriving for talks on Wednesday with President Bill Clinton and Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, Aznar cited Madrid's decision last year to fully join the alliance's command structure.

"With this decision, my government wishes to fulfil its commitments to Western defence, and asks in return that its contribution to it be clearly recognised," he said in a speech at Georgetown University's School of Foreign Service.
Aznar did not spell out what he was seeking in terms of recognition, but analysts in Madrid said Spain was keen to play a more prominent role in the reformed North Atlantic Treaty Organisation.
The focus of Aznar's meetings in Washington was expected to be the expansion of NATO. Madrid will host a landmark summit in July due to open the door to some former Soviet bloc states.

"I believe it is only fair to acknowledge the American contribution to European defence in recent decades," he said in the English-language translation of his speech made available by the Spanish embassy. "And it is our aspiration to ensure that in this new global situation the partnership between Europeans and Americans that has contributed so much to peace will be renewed."

Also likely to figure prominently in his talks is Cuba, a former Spanish colony. Aznar's centre-right Popular Party government, the first right-wing administration in Spain since the dictatorship of Francisco Franco ended in 1975, has won praise from U.S. officials for its hard line against Cuban President Fidel Castro's Communist government.
